newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo c.bank sells more bonds from its portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Yugo c.bank sells more bonds from its portfolio.

text.p: Yugoslavia's central bank has sold a total of 41.05 million dinars ($7.24 million) in bonds from its bond portfolio, the Belgrade bourse reported on Monday.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) put part of its bond portfolio on sale earlier this month to compensate for funds previously given to Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency to finance grain stockpiling.
Out of 88.8 million dinars offered in two tranches of 6-month bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, the NBY sold 31.939 million dinars of bonds last week.
Another 9.11 million dinars were sold in a week to April 4.
The bond's face value is 10,000 dinars and it carries an interest equivalent to the NBY's discount rate set at a monthly 2.5 percent for April.
Although almost half of offered bonds were sold out, traders said investor interest would have been greater if banks were allowed to trade with those bonds among themselves.

"For some reason, probably not to lose control over the paper, the NBY does not allow interbank trading but only banks-to-central bank, banks-to-agency and agency-to-central bank," a trader told Reuters.
Commercial banks pay those bonds from a special reserve requirement account established with the central bank. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
